items.name: Basic lollipop plot

children.text: A lollipop plot displays data points as symbols (like a scatter plot), and connects them to a baseline by vertical or horizontal segments. Lollipop plots are often used as a visually cleaner alternative to bar plots.

Load data from an online source. Aggregated from original source: https://statbel.fgov.be/nl/themas/
mobiliteit/verkeer/verkeersongevallen
Specify which data attributes you want to map to the X- and the Y-position. Set a fixed fill and stroke color using a valid CSS color string. F.ex. #f304d3, #ccc, rgb(253, 12, 134), steelblue.
Transform the plot specification (which describes the plot in JSON format) to graphical objects.
Basic Lollipop Plot
Set a size scale with a custom size range.

Add a legend for the size scale. Set the title and custom visible tick values. Increase the title limit to make longer titles visible. Finally customize the XY position, the title angle and alignment.
Set the title of the Y-axis.
Delete the title of the X-axis.
Add a plot title.

children.text: Custom baselines allow to set a starting point other than zero, which can highlight deviations from a reference value. This is useful for comparing against targets or emphasizing relative changes.
Copy, paste and parse the results of the data preparation steps in a separate network. http://new.nodebox.live/example/data-manipulation
Create a custom sized plot figure. NodeBox Plot nodes do not require a specific order. Changing the plot figure can be done before or after plotting the data.
Set a fill color scale to show if values are above or below mean. Use a custom range.
Lollipop with custom baseline

It is good practice to keep data visualizations up to date by connecting directly to online sources. However, since NodeBox executes every node at runtime in the browser, larger data files and computation-heavy manipulations can slow down your network. In such cases, it is better to perform the data preparation in a separate network.
